messages:
jessica (infra): :rotating_light: eu-central-1 GPU nodepool (gpu-eu-2) is exhausted and CA is oscillating — we have ~40 pods Pending with gpu=1 and several nodes in NotReady. Kubelet logs show repeated oom and `container runtime reaped pid` errors.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-342, priority=P0, paging oncall.
mike (oncall): grabbing node list and events now. show me `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-eu-2 -o wide` pls.
sam (sre): can you paste the CA logs? curious if scale-up requests are being rejected by cloud provider throttling.
jessica (infra): CA logs (tail):
```
I0221 09:12:30 cloudprovider.go:245] Requesting 8 nodes for nodegroup gpu-eu-2
I0221 09:12:31 cloudprovider_aws.go:89] API error: RequestLimitExceeded
I0221 09:12:45 autoscaler.go:563] Scale-down inhibited: recently scaled up
I0221 09:13:05 kubelet.go:412] runtime oom: killed process 2389 (kubelet)
```
mike (oncall): `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-eu-2 -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}\n}{end}'` ->
```
ip-10-0-12-4 NotReady
ip-10-0-12-5 NotReady
ip-10-0-13-7 NotReady
```
anya (mlinfra): top offending pods (by gpu+mem) from `kubectl top pods -A --containers | sort -k5 -nr | head`:
```
realtime-infer-xyz    infer-container   9/1 GPUs  110Gi
batch-hack-abc        worker            1/1 GPUs  48Gi
```
jessica (infra): realtime-infer-xyz looks like a runaway — configured with replica=20 and no resource limits for memory. We should: 1) cordon nodepool 2) scale up a warm pool (smaller instances) in eu-central to give CA room 3) forcibly evict/k8s delete the runaway pods 4) tweak CA scaleDownDelay and maxNodeProvisionTime to stop thrash.
mike (oncall): cordoning nodes in gpu-eu-2 now. `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-4` (done), ip-10-0-12-5 (done), ip-10-0-13-7 (done).
sam (sre): submitting a fast warm pool request to cloud team: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group warm-eu-gpu --desired-capacity 6` — they acknowledged.
anya (mlinfra): killing the top realtime pods by label to free GPU allocations: `kubectl delete po -l app=realtime-infer -n prod --grace-period=0 --force` (started). Expect some job restarts, will patch deployment after.
jessica (infra): while pods die, patching cluster-autoscaler configmap: setting `scale-down-delay-after-add=20m` and `max-node-provision-time=30m` and `expander: least-waste` to prefer smaller instances. Applying now.
mike (oncall): CA config patched. Also temporarily bumped nodegroup quota for gpu-eu-2 with cloud team to allow +8 nodes (request id q-8892).
infra-bot: Alert: node readiness flapping suppressed by incident policy.
sam (sre): observed CA stop thrashing after warm pool scaled. New nodes coming up as Ready: ip-10-0-14-2 Ready, ip-10-0-14-3 Ready.
anya (mlinfra): after killing pods, GPUs freed. Realtime deployment restarted but with new replica=3 patch applied (replica reduction to stop immediate requeue). Patch command: `kubectl scale deploy/realtime-infer -n prod --replicas=3`.
jessica (infra): follow-ups: 1) add resource limits to realtime-infer (mem 16Gi, gpu request 1) 2) create an alert when NodeReady flips >5x in 10m 3) add CA rate-limit/backoff for provider RequestLimitExceeded 4) plan emergency runbook to cordon and warm pool scale. I'll file runbook PR.
mike (oncall): cost note: warm pool + extra nodes ~ +$5k/day if sustained. marking oncost in ticket.
sam (sre): root cause hypothesis: large model update rolled out to realtime-infer changed memory usage, combined with preemptible churn and API rate-limit prevented CA from adding capacity quickly. Need a canary for model pulls.
anya (mlinfra): adding resourceQuota/policy to prevent unbounded mem for GPU workloads in prod. WIP.
jessica (infra): marking incident resolved for now — cluster stable, pods running, CA steady. Will keep follow-ups in INC-2026-342. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
